How a cloud kitchen can take orders on WhatsApp

The Quality Kitchen shows how a menu, portion choices, and a basket can turn browsing into a useful WhatsApp enquiry.

Webly · 9 November 2026 · Food & ordering · 1 min read

Start with the questions customers ask

A catering menu needs to help someone decide what to serve and how much to get. The Quality Kitchen website lets visitors filter dishes and select portions before they talk to the kitchen. That puts the decisions about food first, while the photography gives each dish room to make an impression.

Use the basket to collect choices

Visitors can gather dishes and portions in one place before reaching out. The basket carries those selections into a WhatsApp message. The customer can review the message and send it in WhatsApp, where the kitchen can confirm availability and discuss the order.

Decide what happens after the message

Agree who replies, what they need to confirm, and how payment and delivery will be arranged. A useful handoff tells the customer they are starting a conversation. Test the message on a phone with several items and portion sizes before you share the menu.
